transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-17
Time: 14:00 - 14:58 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Dr. Lenora Hale, Marco Silva, Jin Park (CobaltNeuro)

Summary:
Quick renewal check + scope to add EU on-prem pilot and modest capacity uplift. Customer wants clearer timeline, security artefacts (SOC2, KMS integration), and an initial latency benchmark to sign off on private deployment. Redwood to send revised SOW and pilot plan.

Topics:
- renewal term and retainer sizing
- EU on-prem pilot scope (hardware footprint, networking, KMS)
- security/compliance artifacts and SSO/SAML
- benchmarks: latency, throughput, KV cache behavior
- timeline and responsibilities

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey — thanks everyone for squeezing this in. quick agenda: renewal numbers, eu on prem pilot, and then Diego will walk through the benchmark plan.
[00:18] Dr. Lenora Hale: Thanks Maya. We're, uh, mostly happy but need certainty on cost if we go private for EU workloads. Also, our compliance team needs KMS and audit log detail.
[00:34] Marco Silva: and we need static egress IPs, VPC peering pattern, and an idea of how Redwood handles K-V cache migration if we move traffic.
[00:46] Maya Chen: totally. at a high level we recommended a retainer bump to cover baseline inference and a small dedicated pool + private pilot for eu-onprem. I'll share numbers after this call.
[01:02] Jin Park: timeline question — can we start pilot in august? our product roadmap puts the GA launch late Q4 so we need a pilot earlyish.
[01:17] Priya Kapoor: that aligns with our typical onboarding — 4–6 week pilot if infra is ready. we'll own the onboarding playbook and runbooks.

[05:12] Diego Ruiz: ok i'll jump into the technical. for the eu on-prem pilot we expect a small node group — typically 2x A100-class or 4x H100-similar depending on model family. we support quantized weights to reduce memory footprint, and our runtime does continuous batching and kv cache so latency stays low.
[05:36] Marco Silva: Hmmm. what's the recommended ratio for latency sensitive traffic? we need < 150ms p95 for live scoring.
[05:51] Diego Ruiz: with proper batching and prefix caching you should see sub-120ms p95 for single-turn generation on a 2-node A100 setup for the models you're running. caveat: if you do large context lengths it changes. also the K-V cache is per-node; we can prime it during warmup.
[06:10] Dr. Lenora Hale: when you say "prime" — do you mean we pre-warm with common prompts? how does that interact with privacy/retention?
[06:24] Diego Ruiz: yes, you can seed with common prefixes. for privacy, we don't persist customer data outside their private cluster; logs and KV are in customer-controlled storage when on-prem. small transcription note: some of our docs call it K-V cache, sometimes SEA transcribers put K-V cash in notes — ignore that.

[10:03] Marco Silva: network — we will need a list of required firewall ports, outbound IP ranges, and whether Redwood requires VPN or direct connect. Also can Redwood integrate with our Azure Key Vault or do you require a specific HSM?
[10:22] Maya Chen: we support multiple KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google KMS, and customer HSMs via PKCS11. we'll include an integration guide. For network we support VPC peering or site-to-site VPN; direct connect works too and gives better egress consistency. we'll list egress IPs in the SOW.

[14:41] Jin Park: on pricing: we'd like a blended committed rate for the retainer plus a defined pilot budget. we prefer not to over-commit until the pilot validates latency and per-token unit economics.
[14:57] Maya Chen: fair — what we usually do: a 6–12 month retainer with a pilot addendum that has a separate line item for private pilot (time-limited). if pilot meets objectives you roll into a long-term dedicated capacity commitment with breakout for private hosting.

[20:05] Dr. Lenora Hale: compliance: SOC 2 is a must, and we also need iso audit artifacts and an attestation of where logs are stored. do you have an SOC2 report we can share with security?
[20:19] Priya Kapoor: yes — we have a SOC2 Type II report, ISO docs, and an auditors package for enterprise customers. we'll attach those to the SOW and share a redacted packet for initial review.

[24:50] Diego Ruiz: benchmarks — plan is: 1) run a baseline hosted API test in eu-central-1 with your prompt set, 2) run the private on-prem setup in the customer's lab or co-lo, 3) compare p50/p95/p99 and token cost. we'll instrument token counts with the Console traces and provide per-route breakdowns.
[25:11] Marco Silva: can you simulate our traffic pattern? it's mostly short chat-turn inference but spikes at end of day.
[25:26] Diego Ruiz: yep we'll use your sample traffic and synthetic bursts; also we'll test failover — route to hosted if private capacity is saturated. note that fallback requires compatible model variants, which we'll include in the config.

[30:00] Jin Park: what's the expected lead time to have the private cluster up after we sign the pilot SOW?
[30:12] Maya Chen: once SOW signed + PO and your infra details, typical timeline is 3–5 weeks for on-prem setup including KMS integration, security review and initial benchmark. if it's co-lo with pre-validated hardware it can be faster.
[30:26] Marco Silva: ok, hardware — do you ship an appliance or do we provide the GPU hosts?
[30:34] Diego Ruiz: Redwood Private can be deployed two ways: 1) customer-provided hosts (we provide RPMs/container images and config) or 2) partner co-located appliance where we handle ops. For this pilot we recommended customer-provided co-lo racks so you control networking and KMS.

[36:45] Dr. Lenora Hale: token economics — we need a worked example for our e2e flow. last time the numbers didn't include warm caching benefits.
[36:59] Priya Kapoor: good point — we'll include a runbook showing how caching and batching reduce per-token cost in production vs cold runs. Diego will produce sample numbers from the benchmark.

[41:20] Marco Silva: security question — how granular is RBAC in Redwood Console when running private? we need separate roles for SRE, ML engineers, and product.
[41:33] Diego Ruiz: RBAC maps to your SSO. when private, we can integrate with your SAML IdP and sync groups to role mappings — SRE gets deploy+trace, ML eng gets model rollout and evals, product gets dashboards only. audit logs are forwarded to your SIEM.

[46:05] Jin Park: competitor check — one of our vendors (mentioning Anthropic) said their private option has simpler KMS workflow. how is Redwood different?
[46:19] Maya Chen: our differentiation is production-first: runtime optimizations, smart routing between hosted and private, and built-in fallbacks to keep latency SLOs. on KMS we support HSMs and standard enterprise integrations, so it's not a blocker.

[52:10] Diego Ruiz: a small technical caveat — if you choose aggressive quantization it can slightly change output tokenization and quality. we'll include eval thresholds in the pilot acceptance criteria.
[52:28] Dr. Lenora Hale: that's fine as long as we have quality gates and a rollback path.

[55:02] Maya Chen: okay quick recap and next steps: Redwood to send revised SOW and security pack by 2025-07-21; Marco to send network/KMS details by 2025-07-22; Diego will run and share benchmark plan by 2025-07-28; we tentatively schedule pilot kickoff 2025-08-04. any other items?
[55:28] Marco Silva: none from me.
[55:32] Jin Park: nothing, thanks.
[55:35] Dr. Lenora Hale: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings present (e.g., K-V cache transcribed as "K-V cash"), proper nouns like model family names may be incomplete. speakers sometimes overlap; timestamps approximate.
